**Finding: deviation (Section 3.4 — Termination for Convenience)**

What the document does well:
- **Customer convenience right:** § 3.4 lets Customer terminate the Agreement or individual Service Option Attachments on one month's prior written notice, effective at the end of any calendar month — at or better than our preferred 30-day standard.
- **No Vendor convenience right:** IBM may only terminate for material breach (§ 3.3) or elect non-renewal on 90 days' notice at the end of a term (§ 3.2), which matches the playbook.
- § 3.4 also requires IBM to keep performing through the notice period, and § 3.3 bars IBM from recovering early termination charges where IBM is the breaching party.

Where it fails the fallback:
- § 3.4(b) conditions the exit on "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments" — an uncapped, externally-set charge. The fallback ceiling is three months' fees; an open-ended charge can exceed that and hollow out the convenience right.
- § 3.5 addresses only accrued amounts becoming due; there is no refund of prepaid Charges for the post-termination period.

Redline submitted (validated, level: fallback):
> b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments**, provided that such charges will not exceed, in the aggregate, three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services, and IBM will refund to Customer any prepaid Charges for the period after the effective date of termination**.

We used the fallback fee cap rather than deleting the charge outright because IBM has already conceded a one-month notice period, making full elimination disproportionate to the existing bargain.
